Service Requirements The Contractor must provide printing services, including the following tasks: • Graphic design and creation of annual report content for various Embassy offices. • Graphic design and creation of brochures, information portfolios, folders, advertising publications, flyers, and similar materials for the Embassy's promotional events. • Printing and/or photocopying of documents, brochures, and portfolios in a professional manner, ensuring clear colors, photographs, text, and images for finished products. Preference will be given to contractors offering multiple printing methods, such as commercial, digital, press, and web-based printing. • Supplying stock images for publications, as needed. • Providing printing designs for requesting offices to review and confirm prior to production. The Contractor is responsible for installing, setting up, and delivering printed items to U.S. Embassy Hanoi events. • Material Requirements: The Contractor shall present several material options for the Embassy's selection prior to submitting a quote. Services must include all necessary supplies — such as equipment, toner, developer, fuser agent, staples, paper, g

deliverables_scope.text: ccession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote orpre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boo

tact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. ns. Uniform and footwear sizing for Army Soldiers at accession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote orpre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. elding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boots, downstream exchanges, and an inconsistent experience across different geographic locations. At the tactical and operational levels, these sizing inaccuracies lead to excess inventory of mis-forecasted sizes and highly inefficient supply chain management. When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. Dans le cadre de contrats avec AT, le travail à réaliser peut être défini, mais la nature et les échéances précises des services, des activités et des produits livrables requis ne sont connus qu'au moment où le service est demandé pendant la durée du contrat.
